metadata.title: A critical review and meta-analysis of studies investigating the effects of the professional development teachers typically receive

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This paper is a systematic review and meta-analysis of primary studies using nationally or state-representative datasets (including international large-scale assessments such as TIMSS, PIRLS, PISA, TALIS, ICILS, and others). Because the authors do not re-analyze individual student/teacher microdata, there is no single study-specific sampling-weight variable (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) to extract for the review itself. Instead, the review codes whether primary studies reported and used probability weights, clustering/nesting adjustments, and plausible values when analyzing achievement outcomes. The meta-analysis is conducted on effect sizes (Pearson’s r converted to Fisher’s z) using robust variance estimation and random-effects models, rather than on weighted microdata; therefore, survey-weight handling is treated as a coded methodological feature of included studies, not as an implemented weighting scheme in this review.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values are not applicable because this work does not fit achievement models to ILSA microdata; it synthesizes effect sizes reported in included studies. Missing-data handling is not reported at the level of this review because the authors do not perform a new imputation or deletion procedure on a pooled micro-dataset; instead, they exclude primary studies when insufficient information is available to compute effect sizes (and they attempted to contact authors for missing data).

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: This is not an analysis of a single ILSA micro-dataset. The review identifies eligible primary studies via database searches (ERIC, Scopus, Web of Science) plus hand-searching and reference screening, then applies inclusion criteria: (1) effects of Grades 1–12 teachers’ professional development participation (formal and planned PD activities) on outcomes; (2) effects of PD participation in general (not a specific PD program); and (3) teacher samples representative at national or state level. The final corpus contains 68 papers, and the meta-analysis uses effect sizes from a subset of included studies with sufficient reporting for student achievement and instructional practices.

data.null_fields_interpretation: This record is a review/meta-analysis rather than an empirical ML study on ILSA microdata. Consequently, there is no single ILSA program-cycle-grade-domain dataset to map to student-level ML targets, no per-country student sample sizes for the review itself, and no ML algorithm training/evaluation to extract. The meta-analysis aggregates effect sizes (Pearson’s r/Fisher’s z) from included studies, so PV handling and missing-data handling are not implemented as part of this paper’s own dataset construction.
